text:
ana: quick follow-up from today's all-hands — couple of runtime clarifications i forgot to ask live about batching + cache behavior during canary rollouts.

ana: specifically: how do we avoid large cold-start latencies when a canary lands on a node with a cold KV cache and long warmup kernels?

devon: great q. short answer: we rely on staged prewarm + prefix caching in the router. canary deploys have a prewarm phase that streams a small curated prompt set to nodes.

devon: the prewarm set is ~10 prompts per model size by default, tuned from perf tests. it's not perfect for all workloads but reduces 95p cold-start by ~40%.

sasha: also worth noting we enable shorter microbatch windows during canary to favor latency over throughput. that reduces batching-induced tail latencies while the cache is cold.

mike: can you remind product folks what the visibility is? i.e., how do we show customers this is in-progress vs GA?

devon: product: we surface a 'canary warming' state in the console per-model + per-pool. shows % of nodes warmed and an estimated 95p based on current warmup.

lucy: how deterministic is warmup? if a model has many rare token patterns, will the prewarm help?

sasha: prewarm focuses on common prefixes and typical seq lengths. rare token behavior is hard — you'll still see variance. for those we recommend a targeted prompt set (customer-provided) for Dedicated/private.

ana: second Q: what's the plan for kernel rollout timing vs cache schema changes? we had a couple of ops notes about eviction changes landing close to kernel changes.

devon: good flag. kernel and cache schema changes are coordinated but on different cadence. policy now is: kernel ABI changes require a 2-week canary + opt-in rollout; cache schema incompatible changes require a migration job and a 4-week stagger.

devon: if both are required, we gate kernel rollout until migration completes on >90% of nodes. ops will create a migration ticket and the console shows blocking dependencies.

mike: is there an SLO for migration speed? customers will want predictability.

devon: not a formal external SLO yet. internal target is to finish migrations within 14 days for Hosted pools; Dedicated may take longer depending on customer approval windows.

lucy: what about automatic fallback — if a canary hits high latency, does routing fallback to previous kernel automatically?
devon: yes, we have an automated fallback policy: if 95p latency regresses by >25% for 10 minutes, router marks canary variant unhealthy and routes traffic to fallback. there's a manual override.
sasha: also we record a quality signal (token-level perplexity delta) — fallback can be triggered by perf or quality regressions depending on config.

ana: can you paste the default fallback config?
devon: sure:
```
fallback_policy:
  latency_threshold_pct: 25
  observation_window_minutes: 10
  min_requests: 500
  enable_quality_check: true
  quality_threshold: 0.05  # relative perplexity increase
```

lucy: does min_requests count after warmup or total?
devon: total since canary start. we don't start quality checks until min_requests reached.

mike: ops/biz asks — can we opt to have a non-automatic rollback but an alert instead? some customers want manual control.
devon: yep, rollout profiles include: auto-fallback (default), manual-review, and aggressive-auto (shorter window). teams/customers can pick per-deploy.

ana: last one from me — any new kernel work items that will change batching semantics significantly?
sasha: upcoming kernel v4.2 includes sparse attention heuristics for long-context models; how we batch across sequence lengths will change a bit — we're adding adaptive microbatch bucketing to avoid padding blowup.
sasha: impact: slightly higher CPU in pre-processing but lower token compute on average. latency shape improves for long tails.

devon: implementation note: v4.2 requires router to tag requests with 'seq-hint' so kernels can pick bucketing. router change is behind a feature flag for 2 weeks.

lucy: any migration docs I can send to customers?
devon: i'll drop a doc in the console release notes and tag you. also will add a short FAQ about how to provide targeted prewarm prompts.

mike: thanks all. ana — anything else?

ana: nope — thanks devon/sasha. this helped. i'll follow up with a short thread on the customer comms plan. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deployment status: canary-prewarm jobs enqueued (job-id: prewarm-2026-04-12-77)

lucy: awesome — thanks for quick replies everyone.

devon: np, please ping if you want a deeper sync.

ana: logging this as action items: 1) add console indicator for 'warming' (devon) 2) publish fallback config and FAQ (devon + sasha) 3) comms draft for customers (mike).
